r3_note: Short lesson (~30 min, he steps out at 29:34). The -ish negation slips (D10, D11) fit no bucket - PROPOSE an -ish rule. 10:00-19:00 is mostly Amal explaining non-human plural = feminine singular (not taught yet). MSA numerals (D3, D12) recur.

rows.medi_said: شغلت بيتي. من بيتي؟ لا، شغلت بيتي.
rows.why: He dropped min ('worked my house'), rejected his own من بيتي, and Amal restored it: صح، من بيتي; he repeated من بيتي.
rows.english: Yesterday I worked from my house.

rows.medi_said: شغلت بيتي. من بيتي؟ لا، شغلت بيتي.
rows.why: شغّلت is the make-X form (I ran/employed); 'I worked' is اشتغلت (sheet: work | Eshte8el | اشتغل); Amal only fixed the preposition (A2), so the verb passed - may be the engine dropping the ish-. Same-root form swap = B12 like بسط/انبسط, not vocab.
rows.english: Because yesterday I worked from my home.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; a same-root verb-form swap is grammar B12 per the reader brief, not vocab.

rows.why: He put el- on aa5er before the noun ('the end of'); Amal asked 'Did you add in [el]?' and he dropped it: آخر اجتماعاتي.
He used the plural اجتماعات for the single last meeting; Amal: 'It's one. اجتماع.' and he answered 'You're right'.
Feminine adjective on masculine اجتماع; Amal: 'No, اجتماع is masculine. You don't need a t.' and he said اجتماعي الأخير at 04:50.
Clock time takes el- + the feminine number; Amal recast الوحدة and he repeated الـ واحدة.

rows.amal_said: Mm. No. ... When do we take out the أ in numbers؟
rows.why: A date number with no counted noun keeps its -a (khamse); Amal said No, he fixed to خمسة, and she asked when we drop it (only before a counted noun).
Giving the temperature as a bare number; Amal said 'No. مش خمس.' right after drilling when the -a drops - a number with no noun keeps it; he did not fix it (خمس و، ستة عشر).

rows.medi_said: uh, لازم-- uh, بنحتاج، uh, جعل الكلمة أخير.
rows.why: جعل is MSA (made/put, past); spoken 'put' is 7ott (sheet: put | 7ott | حط); Amal let it pass and only reacted to the meaning.
rows.english: We need to put the word last.

rows.why: أخير is the adjective 'last'; 'put the word at the end' needs bil-aa5er / fil-aa5er; Amal let it pass. My reading.

rows.why: Engine wrote السبع; his 12:07 'I thought you meant adding at at the end' shows he said a plural-feminine -aat adjective; Amal: 'No. صعبة.' (feminine singular for a non-human plural). Gender/number agreement of the adjective = A8; the el- (A7) reading is not supported.
rows.r3_why: Transcript supports A8: his own comment says he added -aat; her fix is the ending, not el-.

rows.amal_said: That's I don't miss. I don't complain.
rows.why: For 'I don't complain' he said the 'miss' verb (sheet: i miss | Bashtaa2 | بشتاق); Amal: 'That's I don't miss. I don't complain.' (sheet: i complain | Ana bashki | أنا بشكي). A different lexical item = tier 1.

rows.amal_said: مهم. Where's the t؟ You keep the t.
rows.why: A negative command uses the YOU-form (t-); he dropped the t; Amal: 'Where's the t? You keep the t.'
He used the zi33ij (annoy someone) shape for 'get annoyed'; Amal gave بنزعج and he said 'There's an N.'

rows.medi_said: maten, uh, matenbisti. ... Don't enjoy it. Matenbisti.
rows.why: In the -ish negation drill he left off -ish; Amal: 'No. Where's your ish?'. B11 is only ma + you-form (never la) - the -ish ending is in no bucket, so PROPOSE.
rows.proposed_rule: A negative verb takes the -ish ending (ma + verb + ish): ma tinbastish fiyo ziyade, bakulish, bahkish.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw it; no bucket covers the -ish ending (B11 = ma + you-form), so PROPOSE per GR-18. t = his first try 25:36 (25:41 is the same line again).

rows.why: Amal recast his ziyad as ziyaade (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة); may be only the dropped final -e (then S4).
